experiment: MINI Cells Experiment 010 — Residual Adaptive Halting Probe

halting_rule.scope: one autoregressive prefix at a time; batch size 1; stage-level early exit
halting_rule.signal: absolute RMS update of the final-prefix readout position (all K tissue cells for 2D)

interpretation.algorithmic: A viable point shows the learned dynamics already expose a state-derived stopping signal; this does not require a learned halting head and is not specific to 2D.
interpretation.causality: Only the prediction after the complete prefix is scored, so the stopping decision cannot inspect future target tokens. Training-time all-position loss requires a finer-grained causal scheduler.
interpretation.runtime: Observed wall-clock includes GPU-to-host scalar synchronization in this prototype. Iteration savings can exist even if the current Python control flow is not faster yet.
interpretation.training: This experiment probes frozen checkpoints. A positive result justifies a later training experiment with randomized depth/stability loss and causal per-position or per-cell adaptive unrolling; it does not by itself prove lower training cost.

question: Can the already-trained 1D and 2D cellular language models stop recurrent computation from their own state-update residual without retraining?
